title: From a phone to the map
goal: A user sends a photo of a street problem, and the report is shown on a public map.

steps.text: The user puts a photo and a place on the report page.
The user sends the report; after a check it can show on the map.
The client sends a new report to the service.
The service stores the photo and record, then a safe photo.
The map page asks the service for public reports.
The service returns public reports to the map.
The user sends a photo and a place from the report page.
The report page sends a new report to the server.
The server stores the original photo as a private file.
The server writes a report record.
A worker blurs faces and plates and stores the safe photo.
The map page asks the server for public reports.
The server returns public reports; the map shows them.

risks: If blur does not work or the photo is graphic, the report is not public.
If there is no place, the server returns an error.
Many flags take a report off the map.
user_impact: Not shown at once: faces and plates are made hard to read first.
A photo not fit for public is not shown.
tradeoffs: Public only after a safe photo: failure means never shown, and not at once.
Originals stay private; cost is two files and a worker.
Photo check is an outside service; form, photo work, and map share one place.

glossary.definition: A chat a user can send a photo and a place through.
Make faces and plates in a photo hard to read.
A photo marked as not fit to show in public.
